## 342490: exact balanced reconstruction, two routes

Primary: Day–Fleischmann–Manea–Nowotka, arXiv1904.09125v2, definitions in section2 and section5, Proposition23, Conjecture24 and full Proposition25 proof read. Their weakly-0-balanced means exactly equal numbers of a and b; the corpus calls this strictly balanced. Multiplicities are ignored. Put h=floor(k/2)+1; the target is equality of sets of subsequences with h a's and h b's for two words with k of each letter. All k>=1 are required. Proposition25 only handles at most two b-blocks (or symmetrically a-blocks). Its case distinctions reconstruct five run exponents; that is an existing public subcase, not a full solution.

Route A: gap vectors. Write w=a^{x0} b a^{x1} b ... b a^{xk}, xi>=0 and sum xi=k. A balanced query u=a^{r0} b a^{r1} ... b a^{rh}, sum rj=h, is present precisely if some selected b-indices 1<=i1<...<ih<=k satisfy
 r0<=sum_{j=0}^{i1-1}xj,
 r_l<=sum_{j=i_l}^{i_{l+1}-1}xj (1<=l<h),
 rh<=sum_{j=ih}^{k}xj.
Necessity follows by locating the selected b's. Sufficiency follows by selecting the required a's separately in the disjoint intervening intervals. Thus the exact all-word task is injectivity of the union of these downward composition regions, not merely recovery of each region if its indexing were known. Overlapping regions erase which b's were selected. Knowing only coordinatewise maxima does not identify their joint feasible tuples. No injectivity theorem for arbitrary nonnegative x with sum k has been proved here. This is the exact unpaid lemma.

Every balanced subsequence with q of each letter, q<=h, extends to one with h of each: retain an embedding and add h-q unused occurrences of each symbol, then read their positions in order. Therefore the supplied spectrum determines all shorter balanced spectra. This useful reduction does not produce highly unbalanced queries a^i b a^{k-i} used in Proposition23: those have k a's and one b, exceeding h a's when k>2. Mere appeal to Dress–Erdos is not a complete bridge.

Route B: greedy prefix induction. If w starts ab, then ab u is a subsequence exactly when u is a subsequence of w after its first two letters: the greedy embedding of ab ends earliest. Consequently equal balanced h-spectra for two words both starting ab give equal balanced (h-1)-spectra of their balanced residual words. The same holds for ba. If k=2m, the residual parameter is 2m-1, whose required h is m; we have exactly h-1=m. If k=2m+1, the residual parameter is 2m, requiring m+1 of each, while we have only m. Thus the odd induction step fails by one of each letter. Worse, if the first b follows a^s with s>1, greedy ab consumes a^s b and leaves an unbalanced residual word, outside the induction hypothesis. An arbitrary first balanced prefix can be long and loses still more query length. Neither parity nor arbitrary initial runs have been repaired. These are proof gaps, not a counterexample.

Strongest contrary case: a general gap-vector separation lemma could be short, use standard tools and still resolve the full conjecture. The source's two-block proof does not exclude that possibility. No routine exclusion is adopted. Source final/companion/corrections and current registry proof/chronology gates remain unpaid. Search bounded nonmatches do not prove worldwide novelty.

## 329404: exact degree-sequence clique packing, two routes

Primary: Treglown arXiv1412.1774v2. Conjecture1.2 is the exact corpus inequality; Theorems1.1,1.3,1.5 and sections2 and4 through Lemma5.3 and the section6.1 outline were read. Section4 actually derives the asymptotic theorem from an absorbing-set theorem and an almost-perfect packing theorem. The long proofs of these auxiliary results in sections6–8 are not fully read. No reliance on an unread auxiliary proof to clear the target.

Set q=n/r, so alpha is d_i>=n-2q+i for 1<=i<q, and beta is d_{q+1}>=n-q. For r>=2 and q>=1 these are the intended nondegenerate parameters. The corpus r=1 makes the subscript n+1 undefined; that endpoint is a domain correction only. In the complement, a perfect Kr-factor is an equitable q-coloring with every class of size r. The hypotheses allow complement degrees approaching 2q-2 on a small tail; ordinary Hajnal–Szemeredi at maximum degree q-1 does not apply. The source's theorem with gamma*n extra slack cannot be specialized to gamma=0: n0 depends on gamma, and fixed finite input n need not exceed n0(gamma,r).

Route A: remove one Kr and induct on q. Remaining degrees are at least d_i-r, while the new alpha threshold equals n-2q-r+2+i. Uniform deletion therefore loses two units at each tight low degree, even before accounting for rank shifts. A deletion argument would work locally if every retained tight low vertex had at most r-2 neighbors in the deleted clique, but constructing a single clique with that simultaneous property is unproved. The beta threshold also changes, and the order of low vertices changes. The source reports an earlier proof when no low-degree vertex lies in a Kr+1; our hypotheses do not impose it. This identifies the difficulty rather than transferring the extra-hypothesis theorem.

Route B: extremal barriers and exchanges. The simplest proposed refutation is a complete multipartite graph with an independent part of size q+1. It has no Kr-factor because each clique covers at most one vertex of this part. But q+1 vertices have degree <=n-q-1, contradicting beta at index q+1. Thus this mechanism fails for an exact mathematical reason. A near-perfect factor with an uncovered set might be repaired by exchanges between cliques, but the alpha inequalities only control sorted degrees, not how the nonneighbors are distributed among the cliques. A vertex can block every candidate exchange in different locations. No alternating-clique reachability theorem ruling this out was established. The source absorption proof pays for such robustness with positive linear slack; its section4 proof cannot supply a zero-slack absorber.

Strongest contrary case: the exact conjecture is stronger than its known asymptotic theorem, and a novel finite barrier or exact exchange argument could be significant. No exclusion from standard tools or size. Exact finite proof/counterexample, final-source equivalence, current chronology and formal route are unpaid.
